requirement.description: RLP encoding and decoding functions have incomplete implementations that cause multiple test failures. The functions return placeholder values ('0x00') instead of properly implementing RLP encoding/decoding logic, particularly for various data types and modes.
requirement.contract: Implement complete RLP encoding and decoding functions that correctly handle integers, strings, lists, and various string modes (text, hex). The functions should properly encode/decode according to the RLP specification and support all test cases in test_rlp_encoding.py.

requirement.description: Missing proper imports and fallback handling for cryptographic libraries (ecdsa, hashlib) that are required for signature-related functions.
requirement.contract: Ensure all cryptographic functions properly handle missing dependencies by either providing graceful fallbacks or raising informative errors. The functions should be able to handle both cases where dependencies are available and where they are not.

requirement.description: The get_created_address function has incorrect implementation for CREATE2 address generation. The RLP encoding for CREATE2 is not implemented correctly.
requirement.contract: Fix the get_created_address function to properly implement CREATE2 address generation according to EIP-1014. The function should correctly encode the salt and init_code data for CREATE2 operations.

requirement.description: The rlp_encode_address_nonce_tuple function has an incomplete implementation that doesn't properly handle the case where data_len > 55, causing it to return early without completing the encoding.
requirement.contract: Complete the rlp_encode_address_nonce_tuple function to properly handle both cases (data_len <= 55 and data_len > 55) for RLP encoding of address-nonce tuples.

requirement.description: The rlp_encode_int function has an incorrect implementation for handling integers greater than 127 that would exceed 55 bytes, leading to wrong encoding results.
requirement.contract: Fix the rlp_encode_int function to properly handle large integers that require multiple-byte length prefixes according to the RLP specification.
